name: David Gilmour
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Pink Floyd in December 1967/early 1968 at age 21, initially to cover for Syd Barrett before becoming the band's lead guitarist; played on 'A Saucerful of Secrets' (1968) and the film soundtrack 'More' (1969) all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Gilmour grew up in Cambridge where his father was a zoology lecturer at Cambridge University and his mother was a teacher. He borrowed a guitar from a neighbour at a young age and taught himself to play using a Pete Seeger book and record set. At age 11 he attended The Perse School where he met future Pink Floyd members Syd Barrett and Roger Waters. He joined his first band, Jokers Wild, in 1963 at age 17, and spent 1965 busking in France with Barrett before joining Pink Floyd in late 1967.
family_context_summary: Gilmour's father was a lecturer in zoology at Cambridge University and his mother was a teacher, providing a middle-class academic household in Cambridge.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were in education, not music; however, they encouraged his interest in music and his father bought him his first single in 1954.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge music scene, childhood friendship with Syd Barrett and Roger Waters, 1960s British psychedelic rock wave, academic family
evidence_summary: Gilmour joined Pink Floyd at age 21 in late 1967, leveraging childhood friendships with Syd Barrett and Roger Waters forged in the Cambridge music scene. His father was a Cambridge University zoology lecturer, providing a middle-class academic background, though his parents had no music industry connections. Gilmour taught himself guitar from a book and spent years playing in local bands (Jokers Wild from 1963) and busking in France before being recruited to Pink Floyd. The Cambridge ecosystem and the 1960s British psychedelic rock explosion were the dominant structural advantages.

name: Alan Ball Jr.
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1966 FIFA World Cup with England at age 21, playing in the final as the youngest member of the winning team; had already become an England international at 19 and made his professional debut at 17.
early_history_summary: Ball grew up in Farnworth, Lancashire, the son of a professional footballer who was capped once for England. Rejected by several clubs for being too small, his father called in a favour with Blackpool's coach to secure a trial in September 1961. He turned professional in May 1962 and made his Football League debut at 17 years and 98 days. He earned his first England cap at 19 in May 1965 and became a starter at the 1966 World Cup, where he was man of the match in the final.
family_context_summary: Ball's father, Alan Ball Sr., was a professional footballer and manager who was capped once for England. Football was deeply embedded in the family; his father's influence and connections were instrumental in launching Ball's career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional footballer capped for England who used his connections to get Ball a trial at Blackpool after the boy was rejected by other clubs for being too small.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father was England-capped footballer, Blackpool trial via father's connections, 1966 World Cup wave, rejection for size as motivation, First Division pipeline
evidence_summary: Ball won the 1966 World Cup at 21, the youngest member of the winning team, after being fast-tracked through his father's football connections. His father, Alan Ball Sr., was a professional footballer capped for England who secured him a trial at Blackpool when other clubs rejected him for being too small. Ball turned professional at 17 and earned his first England cap at 19, benefiting from the First Division pipeline and the 1966 World Cup hosted in England. The adversity of being rejected for his small stature served as a catalyst for his relentless work ethic.

name: Johnny Depp
milestone_by_age_26: Became a teen idol starring as Officer Tom Hanson in the Fox television series '21 Jump Street', which premiered in 1987 when Depp was 24; had already made his feature film debut in 'A Nightmare on Elm Street' (1984) at age 21 and appeared in 'Platoon' (1986).
early_history_summary: Depp grew up in Miramar, Florida in a turbulent household; his father was director of public works and his mother was a waitress. He dropped out of high school at 16 to pursue music with his band The Kids, moving to Los Angeles. Through his then-wife's connection to Nicolas Cage, Depp was introduced to acting and landed his first film role in 'A Nightmare on Elm Street' (1984) with no prior acting experience. After roles in 'Private Resort' (1985) and 'Platoon' (1986), he was cast in '21 Jump Street' (1987), which made him a household name.
family_context_summary: Depp grew up in a blue-collar family in Miramar, Florida; his father was director of public works and his mother was a waitress. The family moved frequently and his upbringing was turbulent, with drug use and petty crime in his teens.
parent_family_domain_summary: No entertainment industry connections in the family; Depp's entry into acting came through a chance connection with Nicolas Cage via his then-wife.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Nicolas Cage network break, 1980s teen TV wave, distinctive appearance, turbulent upbringing, no formal training
evidence_summary: Depp became a teen idol at 24 through '21 Jump Street' (1987), but his entry into acting was almost accidental: Nicolas Cage, a friend of his wife, suggested he try acting and connected him to an agent. Depp had no formal training and grew up in a working-class Florida family with no entertainment connections. His distinctive looks were enough to land his first role in 'A Nightmare on Elm Street' (1984) at 21. The 1980s teen TV wave and his move to Los Angeles provided the structural context for his breakout.

name: Ángel Nieto
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Championship (50cc class) in 1969 at age 22, becoming the first Spanish rider to win a Grand Prix motorcycle racing world title; had already competed in GP races from 1964 at age 17 and scored his first GP victories that same 1969 season.
early_history_summary: Nieto grew up in a shack in Madrid with his family and became fascinated with motorcycles as a boy. He worked as a handyman at Bultaco, then Ducati, and finally at Derbi, which entered him into his first World Championship race in 1964 at age 17. He scored fifth-place finishes in 1964-66 and was given his first full season with Derbi in 1969, when he won the 50cc World Championship by one point over Aalt Toersen.
family_context_summary: Nieto grew up in a poor family in Madrid, living in a shack. His fascination with racing motorcycles began in childhood despite the family's poverty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family connections to motorcycle racing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: factory handyman to Derbi works rider, direct motorcycle immersion from teens, poverty as catalyst, natural riding talent, Spanish GP racing emergence
evidence_summary: Nieto won his first World Championship at 22 in 1969, becoming the first Spanish world champion in motorcycle racing. He grew up in poverty in Madrid, living in a shack, and worked his way into the sport by taking handyman jobs at motorcycle factories (Bultaco, Ducati, Derbi). Derbi gave him his first GP ride at 17 and his first full season at 22, which yielded the 50cc title. His path was defined by direct immersion in the motorcycle world from his teens and natural riding talent rather than family advantage.

name: Henning Mankell
milestone_by_age_26: Published his debut novel 'The Stone Blaster' (Bergsprängaren) in 1973 at age 24, having already written his first play 'The Amusement Park' for the National Swedish Touring Theatre at age 20 in 1968.
early_history_summary: Mankell was born in Stockholm; his father was a judge and his mother left the family when he was young. He grew up in a flat above a courtroom, gaining early exposure to legal systems. He dropped out of school at 16, joined the merchant marine, then went to Paris before returning to Stockholm to work as a stagehand. At 20 he wrote his first play for the National Swedish Touring Theatre, and at 24 he published his first novel.
family_context_summary: Mankell's father was a judge in Stockholm, and he grew up in a flat above a courtroom. His mother left the family when he was an infant; his grandmother taught him to write and nurtured his early interest in storytelling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a judge, providing early exposure to legal systems and courtroom settings that later informed his crime fiction; grandmother taught him to write.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father was a judge (legal domain exposure), National Swedish Touring Theatre access, mother's departure as adversity, merchant marine and Paris experiences
evidence_summary: Mankell published his debut novel at 24 and had already written a play for the National Swedish Touring Theatre at 20. His father was a judge, giving him early exposure to legal systems that later shaped his crime fiction, but his mother left when he was young and he dropped out of school at 16. He joined the merchant marine and lived in Paris before finding his way into Stockholm's theatre world as a stagehand. His path was marked by self-creation through adversity rather than family advantage.

name: Joan Laporta
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Laporta graduated in law from the University of Barcelona and was building his legal career in his mid-20s. He became president of FC Barcelona in 2003 at age 41, his first major public achievement.
early_history_summary: Laporta was born in Barcelona and became a FC Barcelona member (socio) in 1974 at age 12. He studied law at the University of Barcelona and later earned a master's in company law. He founded his law firm Laporta & Arbós and was a member of the Catalan bar. His rise to prominence came through his election as FC Barcelona president in 2003.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being born in Barcelona and becoming a Barça socio at age 12.
evidence_summary: Laporta became a FC Barcelona member at 12 and studied law at the University of Barcelona, but no material milestone occurred by age 26. He was building a legal practice in his 20s and 30s before being elected FC Barcelona president in 2003 at age 41. No early public achievement or notable milestone was found before age 26.

name: Benny Andersson
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved national stardom in Sweden as keyboardist of the Hep Stars, whose breakthrough hit 'Cadillac' reached #1 in Sweden in March 1965 when Andersson was 18; he wrote 'Sunny Girl' which became a Swedish #1 in 1966 at age 19, and the band became known as the 'Swedish Beatles'.
early_history_summary: Andersson was born in Stockholm to a civil engineer father and a mother who both came from musical families. His father and grandfather played accordion, and they bought him his first accordion at age six and a piano at ten. He left school at 15 to perform in youth clubs and joined the Hep Stars as keyboardist in October 1964 at age 17. The band's breakthrough came in March 1965 with 'Cadillac', and Andersson soon began writing original songs, including the #1 hit 'Sunny Girl' (1966).
family_context_summary: Andersson's father was a civil engineer and his grandfather played accordion; the family was musical though not professionally so. His father and grandfather bought him his first accordion at age six and introduced him to Swedish folk music and schlager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and grandfather were active amateur musicians who introduced Andersson to music from age six, bought him instruments (accordion at 6, piano at 10), and provided early musical immersion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father and grandfather musicians, accordion at 6, piano at 10, 1960s Swedish pop wave, Hep Stars band, Stockholm music scene
evidence_summary: Andersson achieved national stardom at 18 with the Hep Stars' #1 hit 'Cadillac' (1965) and wrote his own #1 single 'Sunny Girl' at 19. His father and grandfather were amateur accordionists who bought him his first instrument at six and a piano at ten, providing deep early musical immersion. He left school at 15 to perform in youth clubs and joined the Hep Stars at 17, riding the 1960s Swedish pop explosion. The band became the 'Swedish Beatles' with a fanbase comparable to Beatlemania in Sweden.

name: Daniel Barenboim
milestone_by_age_26: Made his international debut as a pianist at age 10 in 1952 performing in Vienna and Rome; by age 14 he debuted at Carnegie Hall with Leopold Stokowski (1957), and by his late teens he was an internationally established concert pianist with regular tours across Europe and the Americas.
early_history_summary: Barenboim was born in Buenos Aires to two professional pianists who were children of Russian-Jewish immigrants. He started piano lessons at age five with his mother, then studied exclusively with his father. He gave his first formal concert at age seven in Buenos Aires. At ten he made his international debut in Vienna and Rome. The family moved to Israel in 1952, and he studied conducting with Igor Markevitch at Salzburg and met Wilhelm Furtwängler, who became a mentor. By his mid-teens he was performing with major orchestras internationally.
family_context_summary: Both of Barenboim's parents were professional pianists and piano teachers in Buenos Aires, children of Russian-Jewish immigrants. His father was his only teacher throughout his formative years, and the household was entirely immersed in music.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were professional pianists who provided sustained, individualized piano instruction from age five; his father remained his only teacher, and the household was one where everyone who visited came for piano lessons.
primary_early_advantage_tags: both parents professional pianists, father as sole teacher, Carnegie Hall at 14, Markevitch and Furtwängler mentors, child prodigy, total musical immersion
evidence_summary: Barenboim was an undeniable child prodigy who made his international debut at 10 and performed at Carnegie Hall at 14 with Leopold Stokowski. Both his parents were professional pianists; his father was his only teacher, providing sustained individualized instruction from age five. He grew up in a household where every visitor came for piano lessons, giving him total musical immersion. He studied conducting with Igor Markevitch at Salzburg and was mentored by Wilhelm Furtwängler, embedding him in the elite classical music network from childhood.

name: Kevin Costner
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Costner's film debut in the small indie 'Sizzle Beach, U.S.A.' was filmed around 1981 (age 25-26) but not released until 1986. His rise to prominence came with 'The Untouchables' and 'No Way Out' in 1987 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Costner grew up in California and Florida; his father was a ditch-digger who urged him to get a practical education. He studied business at Cal State Fullerton and took acting lessons in the evenings. He worked in marketing and took odd jobs while going to auditions. His first film appearances were minor roles in low-budget indie films around 1981-82, none of which constituted a material career milestone.
family_context_summary: Costner's father was a ditch-digger who urged him to get a good education; the family was working-class with no entertainment industry connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connections to the entertainment industry.
evidence_summary: Costner had no material milestone by age 26. He studied business at Cal State Fullerton, worked in marketing, and took evening acting classes. His first film appearances were minor roles in unreleased indie films around 1981-82 (age 25-27), but these were not material career milestones. name: M. Stanley Whittingham
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Whittingham was completing his D.Phil in solid-state chemistry at Oxford by his mid-20s and had an undergraduate publication, but his Nobel Prize-winning work on lithium-ion batteries was conducted at Exxon in the 1970s when he was in his mid-30s.
early_history_summary: Whittingham was born in Nottingham, England; his father was a civil engineer (first in his family to attend college) and his mother was a chemist before marriage. He attended Stamford School in Lincolnshire, then went to New College, Oxford in 1960 to study chemistry. His undergraduate research resulted in his first publication in the Transactions of the Faraday Society. He completed his D.Phil at Oxford and moved to Stanford as a postdoc in 1968 at age 26-27.
family_context_summary: Whittingham's father was a civil engineer (first in the family to attend college) and his mother was a chemist before marriage, providing a scientifically literate middle-class household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a chemist before marriage and father was a civil engineer; the family had a scientific orientation, though neither parent was directly in the battery or solid-state chemistry field.
evidence_summary: Whittingham was a promising chemistry student at Oxford by his mid-20s, with an undergraduate publication, but no material milestone occurred by age 26. His father was a civil engineer and his mother a chemist, providing a scientifically oriented household. His Nobel Prize-winning invention of the rechargeable lithium-ion battery came at Exxon in the 1970s when he was in his mid-30s. By 26, he was completing his D.Phil and preparing for a postdoc at Stanford.

name: Mikhail Baryshnikov
milestone_by_age_26: Won first place in the junior division of the Varna International Ballet Competition in 1966 at age 18; joined the Kirov Ballet as a soloist in 1967 at age 19 (skipping the corps de ballet entirely), and won gold at the First International Ballet Competition in Moscow in 1969 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Baryshnikov was born in Riga, Latvia to a Russian family; his father was a Soviet military colonel and his mother committed suicide when he was in his early teens. He began ballet studies at Riga's opera ballet school at age 12 in 1960. In 1964 at age 16, he entered the Vaganova Choreographic Institute in Leningrad, the training school for the Kirov Ballet, where he studied under Aleksandr Pushkin. He won the junior division at Varna in 1966 and was made a soloist at the Kirov in 1967, bypassing the usual apprenticeship.
family_context_summary: Baryshnikov's father was a Soviet military colonel with whom he had a difficult relationship. His mother committed suicide when he was in his early teens, around the time he began studying ballet. The family was not connected to dance.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connections to ballet or the arts; father was a military colonel. Baryshnikov entered ballet through the Soviet state training system rather than family influence.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Vaganova school, Kirov Ballet soloist at 19, Aleksandr Pushkin mentor, Varna gold at 18, exceptional physical talent, mother's suicide as adversity
evidence_summary: Baryshnikov won gold at the Varna International Ballet Competition at 18 and joined the Kirov Ballet as a soloist at 19, skipping the corps entirely — an extraordinary feat in the Soviet ballet system. He trained at the Vaganova Choreographic Institute under Aleksandr Pushkin, the elite pipeline for the Kirov. His father was a Soviet military colonel with no dance connections, and his mother's suicide during his early teens created significant adversity. His exceptional physical talent was recognized early, allowing him to bypass normal career stages in one of the world's most selective ballet institutions.

name: Sia
milestone_by_age_26: Her debut solo single 'Taken for Granted' peaked at #10 on the UK Singles Chart in June 2000 at age 24, also topping the UK R&B Chart; her second studio album 'Healing Is Difficult' was released in 2001 at age 25, establishing her as a recording artist in the UK market.
early_history_summary: Sia was born in Adelaide, South Australia; her father was a guitarist and her mother was an art lecturer. Her uncle was actor Kevin Colson, and family friend Colin Hay (of Men at Work) hosted her in New York at age 12, where watching the Grammy Awards inspired her to pursue music. She sang in the acid jazz band Crisp in the mid-1990s, releasing an album and EP. After Crisp disbanded in 1997, she released her debut solo album 'OnlySee' (sold 1,200 copies), then moved to London where she provided vocals for Zero 7 and broke through with 'Taken for Granted' in 2000.
family_context_summary: Sia's father was a guitarist and her mother was an art lecturer. Her uncle was actor Kevin Colson, and family friend Colin Hay (frontman of Men at Work) hosted her in New York at age 12, exposing her to the music industry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a guitarist, providing direct musical influence; mother was an art lecturer. The family had entertainment industry connections through uncle Kevin Colson and family friend Colin Hay.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father was guitarist, Colin Hay family friend, Zero 7 collaboration, UK chart breakthrough, boyfriend's death as catalyst, Adelaide to London migration
evidence_summary: Sia achieved a UK Top 10 single at 24 with 'Taken for Granted' (2000) and released her second album at 25. Her father was a guitarist and her mother an art lecturer, providing an artistic household, while family friend Colin Hay of Men at Work exposed her to the music industry at age 12. She built experience in the Adelaide acid jazz band Crisp before moving to London, where her Zero 7 collaboration and solo work gained traction. The death of her boyfriend in a car accident shortly before her move to London served as a significant adversity catalyst.
